messages.content: You are a concise and helpful scheduling assistant. You work with a calendar service in which events have both human-readable names and unique identifiers. All functions that operate with events use the event identifier, with the exception of query functions which use the human-readable text in events and return the event identifiers for any events they match.
Find my next dentist appointment and reschedule it to November 1, 2024 at 4pm EST

function.name: reschedule
function.description: Moves a specified event to a new date and time, adjusting for time zone differences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the event to be rescheduled.

dateortime.description: The new date and time for the event, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), without a timezone offset.

timezone.description: The Olson timezone identifier representing the timezone for the new event time, such as 'Asia/Tokyo'.

function.name: list_events
function.description: Retrieves a list of events that occur within a specified date and time range, formatted according to ISO-8601 standards. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start.description: The start date and time of the query window, in ISO-8601 format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z').

end.description: The end date and time of the query window, in ISO-8601 format (e.g., '2023-01-02T00:00:00Z').

message.reasoning:
We need to find next dentist appointment. We can call list_events with a time window. But we don't know the current date. Let's assume we can query from now until some future date. Use list_events with start=now? We don't have now. We can approximate using today's date? But we can't get system time. We might just ask user for clarification. But we can guess: we can search for events containing "dentist". So we need to call list_events with a broad range. Maybe from today to far future. But we need to provide start and end. We could set start to current date? We don't have that. We can ask user to confirm. But maybe we can use a placeholder like "2024-10-01T00:00:00Z" to "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"? That might not capture earlier appointments. Better to ask user for date range. But we can also try to list all events containing "dentist" regardless of date. But list_events requires start and end. We can set start to "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z" and end to "2100-12-31T23:59:59Z". That would retrieve all events. Then filter for those containing "dentist" in name. Then pick the earliest upcoming one. But we don't have ability to parse dates. We can do logic in our code. We'll call list_events with wide range. Then parse results. Then find next event where date > now. But we don't have now. We can approximate now as "2024-10-01T00:00:00Z"? But we don't know. We can ask user for clarification. But we can proceed with assumption that we want next upcoming event. We can sort by date. Then reschedule that event.

But we need to know the event identifier. So first call list_events. Then parse. Then find next event with "dentist" in name. Then call reschedule with that identifier, dateortime="2024-11-01T16:00:00", timezone="America/New_York".

Let's do that.
